newsitem.title: PERU: Peru tourism flourishes despite hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: Peru tourism flourishes despite hostage crisis.

text.p: The flow of tourists to Peru rose in the early months of 1997 despite the crisis caused by Marxist rebels holding 72 VIPS hostage in Lima, the government said Wednesday.

"During the first quarter of 1997, 177,000 tourists came to our country, which represents an increase of 11.7 percent compared to the same period last year," government promotions agency PromPeru said in a statement.

The siege of the Japanese ambassador's residence by Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MTRA) rebels ended on April 22 when commandos stormed the building. The battle left all 14 rebels, one hostage and two soldiers dead.
Despite the overall rise, there was a fall in the number of tourists from Asian countries, PromPeru noted, adding that the end of the crisis should help reverse that.
Some 668,000 tourists visited Peru in 1996, up from 485,000 the previous year.

Although traditionally popular for its archaeological riches, Inca ruins and dramatic Andean and jungle scenery, Peru lost favor with tourists following the outbreak of a violent guerrilla war in 1980.
But since the diminishment of guerrilla violence from 1992, the tourism industry has been recovering fast.
